His feed ID was Supervisor Tillweather, male-adjacent, he/him. The two others had not stepped forward. He said, “Janity. We need to talk.” Janity stared, and I watched her pulse increase and her blood pressure drop. She had recognized him. Not just as a B-E supervisor, but she knew him, personally. Farai had stopped when I did. Naja kept moving on her mobility device, following Three, one hand on Sofi’s shoulder and the other pulling Tula along. I had an emotion (gratitude? Something, I don’t know, I’ll figure it out later) that she had followed instructions and at least the three of them would get out no matter what happened next. On our private connection, I told Farai, Go, I’ll deal with it . Farai replied, I can’t leave her now . She said aloud, “Who are you?” Tillweather ignored her, but Janity, not looking away from him, said, “This is my second father.” Farai’s expression turned incredulous. I was glad to see it, because I was confused as hell and it helped that a human was, too. Did he want to come with us? I was checking the cameras around us, but there was no other hostile activity here. (Outside, in the restricted waiting area, Distraction2 was proceeding as planned, with Barish-Estranza and HuntSolas pointing weapons and yelling at each other and Port Security surrounding them.) Tillweather said, “Janity, you know I would never hurt you.” Janity’s pulse accelerated. Her voice rough and trembling, she said, “They killed Uncle Armelle, and Lea and Faris. They said they were going to send me and Tula to contract labor—” Tillweather interrupted, “They would never have done that. And they shouldn’t have said it.” He looked sad that it had happened. Farai looked … I don’t know how to describe it? Horrified realization? She threw an “are you hearing this” look at me. He added, “I’m sorry you were frightened.” He moved forward. “I’d like you to come home with me.” Farai stepped up beside Janity and snapped, “Don’t touch her.” The other two B-E employees, who did not seem any happier with this situation than I was, tensed and looked at me, and I looked at them. (Some distance up the ramp, via Three’s visual, I could see that Naja had stopped to climb off the mobility device and send it back to the nearest corral, and Three was shouldering all the bags despite her objections and Sofi and Tula’s attempts to help. They weren’t close enough to the shuttle yet to make it feasible for me to grab Farai and Janity and run.) Tillweather stopped, frustrated. Still talking only to Janity, he said, “These people are hired killers, employed by your mothers. You can’t trust them.” Farai said flatly, “You knew— You knew they were going to kill Leonide. Your family members. You—” She turned to Janity. “Oh, sweet one, I’m so sorry.” That was when I got it. Tillweather was the one who Janity had told about the safehouses. She hadn’t been foolish or resentful or any of the things Farai had considered, just … trusting. Of an adult human who should have been taking care of her. (It pissed me off and I’m not even a human. It was a good thing Naja wasn’t here, and that we hadn’t let her have a gun.) Shaking, Janity said, “I can’t trust them? You just let them take Tula. Because she’s only my half sibling?” She stepped toward me, threw me a hesitant, worried look. I didn’t know what she wanted, I didn’t know how to deal with any of this. (No matter how much you watch humans on media, this kind of intense emotional confrontation sucks to navigate.) But I really wanted to get out of here, so I said, “It’s time to go.” Janity’s pulse calmed a little, like she was relieved. Like she had been afraid for a moment that we would leave her. She said, “We should go. Farai, let’s go.” “Yes, come on.” Farai took Janity’s hand and headed toward the ramp. I waited to see what Tillweather would do. The two B-E employees were watching him, too. He looked briefly frustrated. There were too many other humans going past us to the ramps for him to start anything, and the confrontation was starting to attract the security drones. He could still call the hostiles from outside the docks. Then he turned and walked away. I followed my humans. I caught up with Farai and Janity on the ramp. Janity was crying, and Farai was comforting her. By the time we reached the shuttle’s boarding lock, Three had already gotten Naja, Sofi, and Tula onboard. It waited outside for us, which was not protocol on a mission like this. It should have gone in first to make sure the shuttle was secure, or kept the humans out here with it until I arrived to take over. But we both knew what was in there, we could feel it on the feed, and we knew there was no way anything would happen to our humans on its watch. As Farai and Janity went through the lock, Three looked at me and said, “ Perihelion -drone is angry that I didn’t follow the plan.” Yeah, I bet. “You know that’s a you problem.” “Oh.” Three was disconcerted. Welcome to the consequences of your actions, Three. It said hopefully, “It can’t be a we problem?” “No, it can’t,” I said. “Get in the shuttle.” I followed it inside and sealed the door behind me. In the main compartment, there were loud high-pitched noises and crying, as Mensah and Farai hugged each other with Sofi sandwiched between them.
